author: Donbot
text_post: So the other day I was hanging out with my female friend who I've been telling you about in the other thread who tried to set me up with her cousin, but it didn't pan out(surprise surprise). We were discussing what I want with my life going forward and for once, we were having a decent conversation getting past the cliché advise(put yourself out there, be confident etc etc). I think she's slowly starting to get my incel(a term she never heard of nor do I call myself that to her) isn't as cut and dry as it may seem. She suggested I get a life coach to help me with my situation and to improve other aspects of my life. While I don't think that's too bad of an idea, there are some road blocks with that. What I really want in my life is no longer achievable, and that's sewing my oats by having a 20s style relationship(I'm going to be 32 in about two months). I would like to at least have some sort of non-platonic relationship with a female, but because I've been burned by rejection so many times, I no longer want to go out of my way to get to that point. If a life coach can help me with anything, let it be to find ways to move past my haunted past and not let my incel define who I am. Other aspects of my life that I can improve on is losing weight and getting a better paying job, which unlike getting a sex and dating life, doesn't require another party's cooperation. If if if I find a partner along the way great, but I don't want to make those improvements with the expectation that it'll land me a girlfriend. Problem is, not having a sex and dating life is the source of my misery, and if I hypothetically found someone tomorrow, I would no longer need to get a life coach, rendering his services null and void. All in all, I'm open to hear this forums opinions on the subject matter. Thanks.

author: Reanimated
text_post: Life coach is such a generic term nowadays.  Technically, some of the things I do with internet marketing can be considered life coaching.  What you really need to do to is examine how good this life coach's own life is.  Can they prove to you that they are healthy, wealthy, have excellent relationships and are overall happy?  What things do you already do better than this life coach?  There's a website called MasterClass which shows you some of the top experts teaching online classes.  Some of the classes are a bit ridiculous but obviously they are going to sell because they are taught by the best.  For example, they have Stephen Curry trying to teach you to be as good of a basketball player as him through online courses as if you are going to magically become an NBA champion by watching videos.  This can be considered life coaching as well.  The bottom line is to just do your research so you don't lose your money to scam artists.  Look up Peter Popoff if you want to see a religious scam artist who sells "miracle spring water" that is supposed to make you rich and cure diseases like cancer.  It's sad, yet hilarious in some ways.  Buyer beware.

author: cerebral_barrier
text_post: Given how people who actually cared about me couldn't help me with DSR or life in general, I highly doubt I'd gain anything from a life coach besides paid moral support.    I can picture it now.   Driving home from a long day's work... I walk through the front door of my house and pick up the electric bill.   I laugh because it's only 60 bucks.   I grab a snack from the kitchen then head over to my computer to play a game.    Suddenly, I hear a voice yelling over a loud speaker outside my house.    I think; "Shit! it's the cops..."   I head towards the door and try to hear what all the commotion is about.     The voice gets clearer...  "That's it, CB!  You're doing great!   Keep on living that life!  You the man!!!"    I walk to the window and give a strained thumbs up sign, then head back to my computer to begrudgingly make the payment...   The voice stops yelling, tires screech and the coach's car drives off...

author: cerebral_barrier
text_post: In my case, no one in my social circle can help me with my life; as I'm doing quite well while they can barely help themselves.  In DSR, there are those who can help me but never do. While a life coach may help you make better life decisions, he/she will not be able to directly affect the decisions others make about you.   For example, with regard to DSR, a life coach will not have the advantage of being able offer evidence of any social proof you may have, in the way friends and family can.   Knowing this, and understanding female nature, I would not advise any man to use a life coach or dating coach as a means of meeting women.   You'd be wasting your money.
